questions.q: How many categories does the Get Data dialog organize its connectors into?
options: Seven — File, Database, Microsoft Fabric, Power Platform, Azure, Online Services, Other
Three — Files, Databases, and Everything Else
Five, matching the five-step workflow
It isn't organized into categories at all
questions.explain: File, Database, Microsoft Fabric, Power Platform, Azure, Online Services, and Other — seven categories covering hundreds of specific connectors.

questions.q: What is "Common data sources" on the Home ribbon's Get data button?
options: A short quick-access list of the most frequently used connectors
The only way to connect to data in Power BI Desktop
A category inside the Get Data dialog
A list of data sources your organization has already connected to
questions.explain: It's a shortcut list. If the source you need isn't on it, selecting "More" opens the full Get Data dialog with all seven categories.

questions.q: No matter which connector you start from, where do you always end up before loading data?
options: The Navigator dialog
Power Query Editor, automatically
The Publish dialog
Model view
questions.explain: Every connector — file, database, web, or anything else — lands you in the Navigator, where you choose which tables/data to load.

questions.q: In the Navigator, what's the difference between Load and Transform Data?
options: Load brings data in as-is; Transform Data opens Power Query Editor to clean it up first
They do the same thing
Load is for files only; Transform Data is for databases only
Transform Data publishes the report immediately
questions.explain: Load imports the selected data directly. Transform Data opens Power Query Editor so you can clean and reshape the data before it's loaded — Chapter 3's subject.

options: A saved connection (source and settings, no data) that others can open to quickly build a report against the same source
A backup of a full Power BI report including all its data
A required file for every data connector
A Power BI Desktop installer file
questions.explain: A PBIDS file stores connection details only, not data. Opening one prompts the user to authenticate and pick tables in the Navigator, making it easy for others to build new reports from the same source.
